title: LTI and auth-provider branching
hook: LTI 1.3, an OIDC bearer, and a leftover API key are three shapes of one inbound token. Pattern matching is how you branch without a stringly-typed if pile.

sections.heading: Model the token as data, then switch
sections.prose: Interviews that mention LTI want to hear that you treat the provider as a closed set of records, not as a boolean isLti next to a nullable jwt. Each provider carries the fields it actually has: issuer and deployment id for LTI, tenant and expiry for OIDC, prefix and hash for an API key. A switch expression over that union (abstract record + derived records, or a single record with a discriminator plus property patterns) returns a normalized AuthDecision. Keep HTTP and ASP.NET out of the method; this is language-level branching you can unit test with records.

snippets.label: Property patterns on an inbound token
snippets.explanation: LTI requires issuer. Bearer requires a future exp. ApiKey matches a prefix. Unknown schemes throw. No default that returns admin.

sections.heading: Combine with, list patterns, and exhaustiveness
sections.prose: After Decide, you may copy the decision with with { Roles = [.. decision.Roles, "proctor"] } for an LTI instructor launch. Incoming LTI custom claims often arrive as a string array; a list pattern can require a non-empty context id as the first element. Put relational checks on exp in the arm or in when, not in a later if that every caller must remember. The production failure mode is a new LMS that sends Version = "1.3.0" and misses the "1.3" constant pattern — match StartsWith in a when, or normalize before the switch.

snippets.label: when-guard for LTI version prefixes
snippets.explanation: Constant "1.3" is too brittle for patch versions. is plus property patterns plus a boolean method keeps the switch arms thin.

interviewTakeaways: Encode providers as data; switch on shape, not on scattered booleans.
Unknown or expired tokens throw or return a failed decision — never a privileged default.
when and helper predicates handle prefix versions that constants miss.
with copies the decision for extra roles without mutating the original.
commonPitfalls: Matching Scheme strings with different casing from the wire.
A _ arm that authenticates as guest.
Mutating Roles on a shared AuthDecision across concurrent requests.

jsTsCorrelations.note: type Token = { kind: 'lti'; issuer: string } | { kind: 'bearer'; exp: number }. TS narrows on kind. C# property patterns are the equivalent without a required tag if you match several fields.
